statement: Each new architecture/board profile shall remain planned until its exact context ABI, startup, timer, interrupt, memory and ownership evidence is recorded.
rationale: Profile files alone do not implement target support.
acceptance: Correct compiler ELF attributes; all integer and enabled FP/SIMD/TLS state tested; nested IRQ policy, rollover/catch-up, priority, noheap/constructors and stack/link overflow pass; logs bind board/bitstream/image/config; unexecuted cells remain unverified.
verification: Per-port compile/disassembly and exact RTL/board matrix with failure injections.
configuration: Explicit architecture/board/configuration matrix; enabled optional state enumerated.
resource_budget: Fixed test stacks/pools and bounded retained evidence per target.
finding: Only RISCue cross-builds; no new architecture startup/context/driver implementation or board execution evidence exists.

title: Native C# host tool targets
statement: Every project C# host tool with Native AOT support shall provide a native publish target and execute natively by default throughout CMake, CTest and firmware auditing.
rationale: Use native executables without requiring a .NET runtime at execution time while preserving C# source and XDoc.
acceptance: Publish audit, tracker and configurator for build-host OS/CPU, never firmware ISA; native_tools builds all; tests and ELF audits invoke executables directly; XML docs emitted beside binaries; reflection JSON disabled with generated metadata; AOT/linker warnings fail; unsupported hosts require explicit managed compatibility selection; Linux native self-tests, tracker import/generation and firmware audit pass.
verification: Native publish logs, executable format inspection, CTest command inspection, all CLI self-tests and RV32 audit/static-contract build using host-native tools.
configuration: RTOS_NATIVE_TOOLS=ON default; OFF explicitly enables managed compatibility; host-specific RID.
resource_budget: Native host tools may use host heap; firmware pools/stacks and noheap audits unchanged; separate host build output directories.
finding: Three C# projects have Native AOT targets and generated JSON metadata; host-specific builds require SDK/compiler prerequisites and only tested hosts can claim execution evidence.

title: Static device registry
statement: The kernel shall register permanent device objects before scheduling and seal a finite registry against runtime registration.
rationale: Stable lifetime without heap.
acceptance: Duplicate identities and exclusive MMIO overlaps fail; unavailable devices cannot open; register-only drivers need no worker.
verification: Future boot-registry boundary review and tests.
configuration: RTOS_DEVICE proposed, off in nano.
resource_budget: Fixed object table and per-device state; zero runtime allocation.
finding: Reviews 001-005 require a sealed device registry; the current thread registry is not a device registry.

title: Minimal driver operations
statement: The driver framework shall define initialize, read, write and typed control operations with explicit context, ownership and result contracts.
rationale: Make small FPGA drivers easy to implement.
acceptance: Missing optional operations return unsupported without MMIO; example register driver needs no queue, heap or hidden thread; callback blocking and bounded-work rules are documented.
verification: Future API review and example-driver checks.
configuration: Optional direct-access driver module.
resource_budget: One permanent object and operations table per device; target size reported.
finding: Reviews 006-010 define a proposed operations interface; existing Ethernet callbacks do not provide this general framework.

title: Whole device transaction lock
statement: The driver framework shall serialize each complete logical device transaction across all thread entry points using the same priority-inheriting mutex.
rationale: Prevent interleaved command/data/status sequences.
acceptance: Concurrent callers cannot interleave transaction steps; normal errors release ownership; aliases follow the same lock; reserved hardware stays owned across completion waits.
verification: Future forced-preemption transaction scenarios.
configuration: Direct locked access default when device sharing is enabled.
resource_budget: One static mutex per serialization domain; no mandatory request queue.
finding: Simplicity pass retains existing service contracts, moves wait internals behind an application header, adds named event waits, and reduces formatter scratch. Host model and cross-link evidence do not qualify external interrupts, UART, SMP or target timing.

title: Bounded priority inheritance
statement: The kernel shall implement owner-aware nonrecursive mutexes with separate base and effective priorities and bounded transitive priority donation.
rationale: Bound priority inversion under fixed-priority scheduling.
acceptance: Donation propagates through valid chains; timeout, unlock and priority change recompute donations; highest effective priority then FIFO selects waiters; self-lock and cycles fail before sleep.
verification: Future inversion, chained donation and cycle scenarios.
configuration: RTOS_MUTEX_PI proposed; dependency required by shared-device locking.
resource_budget: Static mutex objects and thread wait metadata; traversal bounded by thread count.
finding: Simplicity pass retains existing service contracts, moves wait internals behind an application header, adds named event waits, and reduces formatter scratch. Host model and cross-link evidence do not qualify external interrupts, UART, SMP or target timing.

title: Typed MMIO access contracts
statement: The port and driver framework shall validate register aperture, width and alignment and define ordering, endian and side-effect semantics for MMIO.
rationale: Avoid invalid or destructive register operations.
acceptance: Overflowing or out-of-aperture accesses fail before hardware access; read-only and write-one-to-clear registers use appropriate operations; barriers are port-defined; no implicit destructive readback.
verification: Future MMIO fake-backend review and target ordering qualification.
configuration: Per-device register map and per-port ordering hooks.
resource_budget: Compile-time register descriptors plus bounded validation; no heap.
finding: Typed read/write/W1C permissions, alignment failures and no-RMW policies now have host bus-observation tests. BSP ordering, bus faults and target access qualification remain open.

title: Race-free completion wait
statement: The kernel shall atomically enroll device waiters with condition checks and use persistent generation-tagged completion state and one absolute deadline.
rationale: Prevent missed interrupts and stale completion reuse.
acceptance: Completion before or during wait enrollment is preserved; wake rechecks predicate; old generations cannot complete new commands; retries do not extend deadline.
verification: Future interrupt-at-each-boundary and timeout-race scenarios.
configuration: Per-device completion predicate and finite deadline.
resource_budget: Static completion generation, predicate and waiter metadata.
finding: Reviews 026-030 require a new wait protocol; existing relative thread sleep is insufficient for device completion.

title: Explicit ISR operation boundary
statement: The kernel shall provide separately named nonblocking ISR-safe operations with bounded work and deferred rescheduling at interrupt exit.
rationale: Keep peripheral interrupts responsive and context-safe.
acceptance: Blocking APIs reject interrupt context; BSP documents acknowledge and nesting; higher-priority unblocked thread runs at the permitted boundary; peripheral IRQ capability remains unavailable until dispatch exists.
verification: Future external-interrupt dispatch and nesting qualification.
configuration: Per-port external interrupt support explicitly enabled only when qualified.
resource_budget: Static handlers and bounded deferred state; no ISR heap.
finding: Reviews 031-035 preserve the current timer-only interrupt limitation and do not claim an implemented ISR IPC API.

title: AXI timeout and fault isolation
statement: The driver framework shall distinguish lock timeout, device completion timeout and AXI access failure and keep uncertain hardware faulted until owned recovery establishes quiescence.
rationale: Software cannot recover every stalled hardware bus access.
acceptance: FPGA integration specifies bounded bus error response or independent timeout; partial commands fault device; reset requires ownership and IRQ quiescence; no timeout is treated as proof that hardware stopped.
verification: Future stalled-device and interconnect fault qualification.
configuration: Board-specified AXI error responder, timeout and reset policy.
resource_budget: Static fault state and counters; hardware timeout resource declared separately.
finding: Reviews 036-040 require hardware-level progress support; thread deadlines alone cannot bound a CPU-stalling MMIO load.

title: Optional queued device service
statement: The driver framework shall optionally serialize slow operations through a statically provisioned request queue and worker with explicit data lifetime and cancellation rules.
rationale: Support slow devices without penalizing simple register drivers.
acceptance: Queue and worker are opt-in; capacity exhaustion returns full; ordering policy is documented; retained data stays valid; queued cancellation differs from cancellation after issuing hardware commands; DMA remains deferred.
verification: Future worker ownership and cancellation scenarios.
configuration: Optional worker, capacity and FIFO or priority policy.
resource_budget: Fixed request storage plus explicit worker control block and stack.
finding: Queued UART service now has host acceptance for producer copies, admission failure, partial writes, budgets, transport error recovery and ISR rejection. Board ownership and hardware timing remain unqualified.

title: Typed static message queue
statement: The kernel shall provide fixed-capacity Queue<T,N> objects for positive N and initially trivially copyable messages with copied ownership and FIFO message order.
rationale: Simple allocation-free communication between threads.
acceptance: Successful send copies payload before return; receive preserves message order; no constructors or allocator calls hide in transfer; target payload, alignment, control and waiter costs are reported.
verification: Future queue ownership, boundary and footprint scenarios.
configuration: RTOS_QUEUE proposed; capacity and message type fixed at boot.
resource_budget: N times sizeof(T) plus exact control/alignment and static wait metadata.
finding: Simplicity pass retains existing service contracts, moves wait internals behind an application header, adds named event waits, and reduces formatter scratch. Host model and cross-link evidence do not qualify external interrupts, UART, SMP or target timing.

title: Timed queue transfer semantics
statement: The kernel shall provide immediate and timed queue send and receive with priority-ordered waiters, FIFO ties and exactly one transfer-or-timeout outcome.
rationale: Predictable blocking with no stolen grants.
acceptance: NoWait returns full or empty immediately; receive failure preserves output; transfer and timeout serialize; selected waiter owns the granted slot or message before competitors can steal it.
verification: Future queue full, empty, handoff and simultaneous-timeout scenarios.
configuration: NoWait, bounded timeout and documented indefinite-wait option.
resource_budget: Wait state lives in permanent thread metadata; no per-wait allocation.
finding: Correctness pass adds host regressions for deadline ordering, wait cleanup, multiple owner-dead waiters, formatter bounds and concurrent logger producers as applicable. Source and host-model evidence does not qualify target interrupts, UART, SMP or timing.

title: ISR-safe queue transfer
statement: The kernel shall provide bounded nonblocking queue operations for supported interrupt contexts using a verified port synchronization protocol.
rationale: Allow IRQ completion messages without sleeping.
acceptance: ISR send and receive return full or empty explicitly; nested producers preserve indices and ownership; no overwrite or unbounded retry; configurable payload cap bounds ISR copy work.
verification: Future nested-interrupt queue and work-bound qualification.
configuration: Explicit ISR transfer methods and maximum ISR message bytes.
resource_budget: Same fixed queue storage plus port critical-section state.
finding: Simplicity pass retains existing service contracts, moves wait internals behind an application header, adds named event waits, and reduces formatter scratch. Host model and cross-link evidence do not qualify external interrupts, UART, SMP or target timing.

title: Event flag wait semantics
statement: The kernel shall provide fixed-width event flags with validated masks, wait-any, wait-all, returned observed bits and atomic optional clear-on-success.
rationale: Express persistent readiness conditions without payload queues.
acceptance: Zero and unsupported masks fail unchanged; timeout consumes no bits; repeated sets coalesce; wait-all requires all requested bits; counting use cases are directed to semaphores.
verification: Future mask, any/all and clear-on-success scenarios.
configuration: RTOS_EVENTS proposed; documented usable mask and clear mode.
resource_budget: One static flag word and bounded waiter metadata per event object.
finding: Correctness pass adds host regressions for deadline ordering, wait cleanup, multiple owner-dead waiters, formatter bounds and concurrent logger producers as applicable. Source and host-model evidence does not qualify target interrupts, UART, SMP or timing.

title: Event wake and payload ordering
statement: The kernel shall serialize event updates and wait enrollment and define priority consumption and broadcast behavior separately.
rationale: Prevent lost updates and ambiguous multi-waiter consumption.
acceptance: Non-clearing waits evaluate a documented snapshot; consuming waits evaluate by priority and remaining bits; ISR set never blocks; payload ownership and visibility require an explicit separate contract.
verification: Future multi-waiter clear, broadcast and ISR-set scenarios.
configuration: Explicit broadcast versus consuming wait policy.
resource_budget: Fixed event state and existing thread wait metadata.
finding: Correctness pass adds host regressions for deadline ordering, wait cleanup, multiple owner-dead waiters, formatter bounds and concurrent logger producers as applicable. Source and host-model evidence does not qualify target interrupts, UART, SMP or timing.

title: Bounded counting semaphore
statement: The kernel shall provide statically allocated counting semaphores with validated initial and maximum counts, bounded waits and direct priority waiter handoff.
rationale: Count work or resource availability without ownership confusion.
acceptance: Overflow fails unchanged; release grants selected waiter before exposing count to contenders; timeout cannot duplicate tokens; ISR release is nonblocking; semaphore has no ownership or priority inheritance.
verification: Future count conservation and release-timeout race scenarios.
configuration: RTOS_SEMAPHORE proposed; boot-fixed initial and maximum counts.
resource_budget: Fixed count, maximum and waiter metadata; zero heap.
finding: Correctness pass adds host regressions for deadline ordering, wait cleanup, multiple owner-dead waiters, formatter bounds and concurrent logger producers as applicable. Source and host-model evidence does not qualify target interrupts, UART, SMP or timing.

title: Bounded thread wait lifecycle
statement: The kernel shall track at most one active blocking operation per thread initially and remove wait membership exactly once on grant, timeout or supported termination.
rationale: Keep scheduler and IPC object state consistent.
acceptance: Blocking before start or from idle fails; timeout range respects modular tick limits; stale wake cannot affect a later wait; internal links are not application-owned; each path removes one wait registration.
verification: Future wait-state transition and stale-wakeup scenarios.
configuration: One active wait per thread; supported finite tick range documented.
resource_budget: Permanent thread wait metadata with bounded object lookup.
finding: Correctness pass adds host regressions for deadline ordering, wait cleanup, multiple owner-dead waiters, formatter bounds and concurrent logger producers as applicable. Source and host-model evidence does not qualify target interrupts, UART, SMP or timing.

title: Abandoned device ownership
statement: The kernel shall report owner-dead and fault a device when its mutex owner exits during an uncertain transaction until explicit recovery restores a safe state.
rationale: Avoid exposing partially programmed hardware as ready.
acceptance: Waiters receive distinct failure; no implicit successful unlock; donation and wait references are removed; recovery requires ownership; fatal corruption is not promised recoverable.
verification: Future owner-exit at each transaction boundary scenarios.
configuration: Explicit owner-dead recovery policy; no dynamic thread reclamation.
resource_budget: Static abandonment and recovery state; no reallocation.
finding: Correctness pass adds host regressions for deadline ordering, wait cleanup, multiple owner-dead waiters, formatter bounds and concurrent logger producers as applicable. Source and host-model evidence does not qualify target interrupts, UART, SMP or timing.

title: Device and IPC metrics
statement: The kernel shall copy coherent bounded device and IPC snapshots into caller-provided storage with separate contention, capacity, timeout and fault statistics.
rationale: Expose contention and resource sizing to applications.
acceptance: Snapshots include mutex owner and effective priority, waiter counts, queue capacity/depth/high-water, full results, timeout/error/recovery; counters saturate safely; count-only query allocates nothing.
verification: Future snapshot coherence and saturation scenarios.

finding: Simplicity pass retains existing service contracts, moves wait internals behind an application header, adds named event waits, and reduces formatter scratch. Host model and cross-link evidence do not qualify external interrupts, UART, SMP or target timing.

title: Modular synchronization configuration
statement: The build configuration shall independently enable device, queue, event, semaphore and mutex modules with validated dependencies and explicit single-hart support limits.
rationale: Preserve the minimal footprint and a future multiprocessor seam.
acceptance: Nano disables all new modules; invalid dependencies fail configuration; disabled storage disappears; IRQ masking is never advertised as an SMP lock; CMake and C# XDoc policies remain in force.
verification: Future configuration matrix and target footprint audits.
configuration: Proposed RTOS_DEVICE, RTOS_QUEUE, RTOS_EVENTS, RTOS_SEMAPHORE and RTOS_MUTEX_PI.
resource_budget: Disabled features contribute zero module storage; enabled sizes measured per target.
finding: Synchronization implementation pass supplies source and host state-machine fixtures; single-hart firmware cross-link is separate from hardware qualification. External IRQ dispatch, board drivers, per-primitive configuration and full acceptance evidence remain incomplete.

title: Small bounded logging and documentation
statement: The kernel shall keep optional static logging capacity configurable, use drop-new initially, bound synchronous drain work and document all proposed APIs and deferred DMA scope honestly.
rationale: Avoid a mandatory 31 KiB log queue and ambiguous lifetime claims.
acceptance: Depth and payload have explicit costs; truncation and full losses differ; buffers remain owned until consumed; ISR formatting is context-safe; no unverified RAM saving or DMA cancellation claim appears in the manual.
verification: Future logging capacity, drain budget and ownership scenarios.
configuration: Logging off in nano; explicit fixed depth and message bytes.
resource_budget: Depth times actual slot size plus formatting and synchronization metadata reported separately.
finding: Correctness pass adds host regressions for deadline ordering, wait cleanup, multiple owner-dead waiters, formatter bounds and concurrent logger producers as applicable. Source and host-model evidence does not qualify target interrupts, UART, SMP or timing.

title: Optional simple FPGA DMA driver
statement: The BSP shall optionally support one selected FPGA DMA engine after interrupt and IPC prerequisites, with one active transfer per channel and fixed aligned buffers.
rationale: Provide bulk transfer without growing the mandatory nano kernel.
acceptance: Driver serializes thread callers; interrupt completion signals a waiter; invalid alignment, length or busy channel fails unchanged; scatter/gather, cyclic transfers and automatic exit cancellation remain excluded initially; disabled DMA adds no driver storage.
verification: Future selected-engine transfer and configuration qualification.
configuration: Proposed RTOS_DMA optional, off in nano; actual engine selected by BSP.
resource_budget: Static channel state and explicit buffer capacities/alignment; report exact target costs.
finding: Portable DMA staging implementation and host binding-rejection tests now linked. A real FPGA DMA engine, IRQ integration and board fault/timing qualification remain open.

title: DMA buffer ownership and quiescence
statement: The DMA driver shall retain exclusive hardware buffer ownership until verified completion or proven quiescence and quarantine uncertain transfers after timeout or owner exit.
rationale: Prevent memory corruption from late hardware writes.
acceptance: Timeout alone never releases a buffer; recovery proves engine stop/reset before reuse; stale completion cannot release a newer transfer; errors and quarantine are observable; no unbounded abort wait is permitted.
verification: Future timeout, delayed completion, reset and owner-exit fault scenarios.
configuration: Per-engine bounded completion/reset policy; no generic cancellation promise.
resource_budget: Fixed ownership/generation and quarantine state; retained buffers remain charged to static budget.
finding: Host acceptance covers receive alias/copy rules plus failed stop quarantine, repeated recovery, malformed completion and unpublished failed-launch tickets. Real engine quiescence and target cache/IRQ timing remain unqualified.

title: DMA address and cache contract
statement: The BSP shall define DMA-reachable bus address ranges, width, alignment, cache maintenance and ordering independently from CPU virtual or physical pointer representation.
rationale: Make DMA portable across FPGA and ARM memory systems.
acceptance: Overflowing or unreachable ranges fail before launch; cache operations respect complete owned cache lines; direction and barriers are explicit; unsupported coherency or addressing fails configuration; no IOMMU is assumed.
verification: Future BSP mapping review and coherency qualification.
configuration: Selected engine and memory-region manifest; coherent or maintained buffers explicit.
resource_budget: Static aligned regions and mapping metadata; cache-line padding reported.
finding: Host tests enforce cache-line capacity, alignment, bus windows, CPU range and channel-metadata isolation; real cache-maintenance and bus-address qualification remain BSP obligations.

title: Conditional SpaceVPX PCIe transport
statement: The BSP plan shall treat PCIe over SpaceVPX as a conditional optional transport with explicit endpoint or root-port scope and a required hardware integration manifest.
rationale: Allow FPGA inter-board communication without assuming topology or compliance.
acceptance: Manifest records IP/revision, role, generation, lanes, slot profile, peer, BAR/windows, address width, IRQ, reset and performance budgets; endpoint registers may precede DMA; root-port enumeration is separately scoped; no SpaceVPX qualification is implied.
verification: Future hardware selection and interface design review.
configuration: Proposed RTOS_PCIE off by default; role and IP remain undecided.
resource_budget: Declared BAR/control storage only; root-port tables and DMA buffers separately budgeted.
finding: Possible SpaceVPX PCIe communication is recorded as conditional architecture work, not an implemented or selected board target.

title: Versioned peer communication protocol
statement: The PCIe transport shall define a versioned fixed-width register/mailbox protocol with explicit endian, bounds, ordering, ownership and backpressure before bulk DMA is enabled.
rationale: Keep peer communication independent of compiler layout and local addresses.
acceptance: Incompatible versions fail safely; lengths and ranges validate without overflow; native pointers and C++ layouts never cross the link; reset generations reject stale responses; synchronization follows actual bridge semantics.
verification: Future peer conformance and malformed-message scenarios.
configuration: Static mailbox depth and message bounds; register-only mode supported where hardware permits.
resource_budget: Fixed mailbox storage and protocol state; no mandatory DMA buffers.
finding: A PCIe bridge does not supply an application messaging protocol; wire layout and peer contracts remain to be designed.

title: PCIe fault and DMA window isolation
statement: The PCIe BSP shall bound accessible peer and local windows and preserve ownership through link loss, reset and uncertain outstanding DMA until quiescence is established.
rationale: Contain malformed peer requests and late transactions.
acceptance: Reject out-of-window access before submission; link loss faults pending work; buffers remain reserved until hardware-specific recovery proves safety; reconnect rejects stale generations; IRQ and posted-write ordering follow selected IP; fault counters are exposed.
verification: Future link-drop, reset, range-validation and late-write qualification.
configuration: Board-specific windows, interrupt mechanism and reset/quiescence policy.
resource_budget: Static window, request-generation and health records; quarantine budget explicit.
finding: PCIe reset and link loss require a selected hardware contract; software timeouts and address checks alone do not establish isolation.

title: Single-hart atomic RAM words
statement: The kernel shall provide 32-bit RAM load, store, exchange, compare-exchange, fetch-add and bitwise fetch operations with interrupt serialization by default, and an independent default-off RISCue Zaamo word-RMW backend, without libatomic or heap dependencies.
rationale: Support small shared counters and flags on RV32 without the A extension.
acceptance: All access uses the object; compare mismatch updates expected; unsigned addition wraps; nested critical state restores correctly; documentation excludes MMIO, DMA and SMP semantics; native target allocator audit remains clean.
verification: Host operation/HAL fixtures and matched baseline/Zaamo real-kernel RTL runs with ticket, bit-ownership, exchange-history, compare-exchange, interrupt and guard checks; physical target qualification remains separate.
configuration: RTOS_SYNC; current single-hart ports. RTOS_ZAAMO defaults OFF and requires RISCue firmware plus explicit atomic-capable RAM; separate matched baseline and feature builds.
resource_budget: One 32-bit word plus alignment; bounded interrupt masking and no runtime allocation.
finding: Default API remains single-CPU. Optional RMW HAL emits reviewed aqrl word AMOs without LR/SC; load/CAS retain local critical sections. Both matched native-RAM RTL runs passed exact totals and guard checks; cross-master ordering, physical timing and SMP remain outside this evidence.

title: Bounded queued printf formatting
statement: The logger shall format a documented integer/string subset into private bounded storage and publish complete copied records without holding a formatting lock or waiting for UART output.
rationale: Provide useful concurrent diagnostics with explicit memory and latency limits.
acceptance: Support documented conversions with matched varargs; reject unsupported format without enqueue; cap format and string scans; report truncation/full; retain pending bytes across partial writes; ISR path accepts preformatted bytes only; physical UART integration remains separate.
verification: Host format/queue/backpressure fixtures, RV32 static-only link and future target stack/latency/UART qualification.
configuration: RTOS_LOGGING requires RTOS_SYNC; fixed logger depth and record size.
resource_budget: RV32 Logger of 8 records with 64 message bytes occupies 720 bytes in the measured example; private formatter consumes reserved thread stack space.
finding: Directed host acceptance covers embedded-NUL records, nonrecursive format data, invalid modifier rejection and exact-capacity bounds; target stack/timing and all backend qualifications remain open.

title: Simple application starting surface
statement: The project shall provide a short application guide and optional convenience header showing copied messages, scoped device transactions and queued printf while preserving existing low-level APIs.
rationale: Keep the small RTOS approachable without removing useful optional mechanisms.
acceptance: One header exposes enabled services without automatic allocation; named event waits avoid positional mode booleans; existing signatures remain valid; a small console example cross-links with a labeled counting sink and explicit board clock replacement; detailed ISR and ownership contracts remain accessible.
verification: Public-header host fixtures, console firmware link/audit, documentation build and future board integration.
configuration: RTOS_SYNC and optional RTOS_LOGGING; existing nano remains feature-off.
resource_budget: Convenience includes have no independent runtime storage; example objects and stacks are statically reserved.
finding: Simplicity pass supplies a short starting path and compatible named APIs; hardware UART, IRQ, clock and timing qualification remain outstanding.

title: Annotated sources and minimal application build
statement: The project shall publish commented C++ contracts, a complete current-port assembly explanation and a reproducible minimal application build in its Sphinx manual.
rationale: Keep implementation ownership and machine-state assumptions reviewable without a separate undocumented startup boundary.
acceptance: Sphinx includes actual source listings; every startup/context instruction has a meaningful comment; frame offsets match the constructor; the nano walkthrough identifies clock and map inputs, commands, ELF/map outputs and memory inspection; native and firmware checks pass without claiming board execution.
verification: Strict Sphinx build, source/frame review, cross-build and comparison of emitted assembly text; target register preservation remains a separate gate.

resource_budget: Comments and host-side manual add no firmware objects; example retains one static application stack and control block.
finding: Source comments, live Sphinx listings and a complete nano walkthrough are present; documentation and cross-build checks do not establish physical timer, register or stack correctness.

title: Source-backed HTML developer guide
statement: The project shall generate a standalone how-it-works HTML guide covering scheduling, application builds, driver ownership and the current assembly boundary.
rationale: Explain the kernel and driver workflow without losing source or resource traceability.

title: FPGA port hardware handoff validation

rationale: Unknown soft cores and maps must not be mistaken for runnable firmware support.

statement: The RISCue build shall expose a validated boot-stack reserve and derive the footprint reserve from final linker symbols.
rationale: Reduce conservative RAM reservations transparently without claiming unqualified stack safety.

title: Ground-linked diagnostic packages
statement: The optional diagnostic service shall accept ground-linked flat images for a boot-reserved execution slot without target ELF parsing or symbol resolution.
rationale: Upload small diagnostics or a shell while retaining ELF and debug symbols on the ground.

acceptance: Precreated worker and scratch capacity; bounded authenticated transfer according to mission policy; digest alone is not authentication; no retained overlay callbacks; explicit states; cache publication hook required; failed transfers stay inactive; hung-code recovery uses qualified watchdog/reset.
verification: Future transfer state-machine and stale-reference checks, cache publication review and hardware fault recovery exercises.

title: Board-qualified QSPI boot and XIP
statement: A QSPI boot target shall distinguish flash storage with RAM copy from memory-mapped execute-in-place and declare its actual startup and flash-busy contract.
rationale: Use nonvolatile storage without overstating RAM savings or assuming SPI implies instruction fetch support.
acceptance: Verify reset path, instruction-fetch mapping, flash mode, cache/latency and erase/program behavior; XIP linker separates load and execution addresses and startup copies writable data; code required during flash busy resides in safe memory; publish measured RAM only after cross-link and board validation.
verification: Future board memory-map review, boot/data-copy execution, flash-busy interrupt exercises and measured footprint.

title: Three-worker PLAIN RISCue AXI UART simulation
statement: The project shall provide a static three-worker UART demo executing actual firmware on the existing PLAIN RISCue AXI core with C# SharpTestBench serial verification.
rationale: Observe repeated work and preemption end to end instead of relying only on host kernel models.
acceptance: Equal-priority workers retain independent arithmetic state; first records show all workers began during non-yielding work; decode physical UART bits and verify repeated per-thread sequence/results; detect fatal/unexpected traps; preserve exact source and binary identities; use no custom Python tooling.
verification: Native C# runner, actual RV32 cross-build/allocation audit, Verilator execution and SharpTestBench UART arithmetic/preemption checks.
configuration: Optional RTOS_SIMULATION host tools; uart firmware preset with SYNC, LOGGING, METRICS, guards and round robin; PLAIN CPU and ordinary simulation RAM.
resource_budget: Three permanent 1536-byte worker stacks, 512-byte idle stack, fixed logger and 4096-byte boot reserve; measure the larger final demo separately from nano.

title: Bounded Cortex-M3 real-kernel IPC stress
statement: The project shall provide a boot-static Cortex-M3 simulation port and bounded stress campaign exercising actual thread context switches, FIFO messages, semaphore handoffs, timeouts and priority-inheriting mutexes.
rationale: Host state models do not execute architecture exception entry or suspended thread stacks.
acceptance: Execute QEMU MPS2 AN385 with three virtual timer timings; verify message sequence/payload conservation, token conservation, contention, low-owner priority donation, CPU-load preemption, finite deadlines and stack sentinels; fail on timeout, guest failure or missing success marker; retain logs and firmware hash.
verification: Native C# runner, Cortex-M3 firmware link and no-heap audit, three QEMU guest runs and existing host regressions.
configuration: Optional RTOS_ARM_SIMULATION; arm-stress preset with SYNC, metrics, guards and round robin; one privileged Cortex-M3 with SVC/SysTick and no external IRQ dispatch.
resource_budget: Nine permanent 2048-byte application stacks, 1024-byte idle stack, eight-slot FIFO, fixed synchronization objects and 4096-byte exception/boot reserve; no target heap.
finding: Added a dedicated simulation BSP with a documented 72-byte integer frame and BASEPRI/SVC enqueue-and-park contract; simulation does not qualify VORAGO hardware, FPU, external IRQs or worst-case stack/latency.

title: Opt-in bounded stack watermark observations
statement: The kernel shall provide opt-in boot stack painting and explicit budgeted stack observations without adding per-thread storage or scanning in scheduling paths.
rationale: Measured observations support stack budgeting without confusing paint with a guaranteed free-space proof.
acceptance: Paint before context creation; scan at most floor(budget_bytes/4) words plus a separate guard check; reject unregistered identities without output mutation; report disabled and incomplete observations explicitly; cover bounds and ARM worker stacks.
verification: Host scanner boundary matrix, ARM real-stack observations, no-heap audit and feature-off cross-build.
configuration: RTOS_STACK_WATERMARK defaults off; explicit stack_usage scan budget defaults to 256 bytes.
resource_budget: No target heap and no new thread-control fields; constant result storage; scan work bounded by caller budget and registered extent.
finding: Watermark scans are separate from ordinary snapshots and dispatch. Paint collisions and unwritten reserved frames remain documented limits; full scans require an explicit interrupt-latency allowance.

title: Bounded simulation subprocesses and dependency identities
statement: Simulation runners shall bound child execution and redirected-output draining, preserve bounded partial diagnostics, and identify verification/runtime dependencies before publishing passing evidence.
rationale: A child exit does not close descendant-held pipes and a main-assembly hash does not identify its dependencies.
acceptance: Native process fixtures cover exit propagation, timeout, inherited pipes and output cap; UART manifests include managed/native/runtime dependencies and reject changed identities; native-tool fingerprints include shared sources.
verification: Native C# process fixtures and actual ARM/UART simulation reruns.
configuration: Native AOT C# runners with XDoc; one deadline for exit and drains, bounded cleanup and eight-million-character output cap.
resource_budget: Host-only bounded capture; no firmware RAM, heap or thread changes.
finding: Panel-050 timeout and dependency-identity findings are addressed in shared orchestration and per-run managed outputs; ignored raw evidence still needs final packaging.

title: Cross-port initialization and allocator rejection contracts
statement: Implemented firmware ports shall reject unsupported initializer, preinitializer and finalizer sections including priority subsections and run positive and negative compiler contracts for their selected ISA.
rationale: Silent orphan initializer sections and incomplete symbol patterns undermine constant-initialization policy.
acceptance: Both linkers reject array subsection variants despite section GC; native audit recognizes dotted constructor and reentrant allocator names; ARM and RV32 static_contract_check run compiler-negative fixtures.
verification: Native C# symbol self-tests and real ARM/RV32 compiler-linker fixtures.
configuration: Architecture-selected static_contract_check; no default libc or libgloss linking.
resource_budget: Host fixtures only; no target heap or runtime constructor machinery.
finding: Panel-050 ARM linker hole is repaired with wildcard retention and explicit assertions; the symbol audit is a complementary known-name check rather than proof against renamed allocators.

title: ARM register and alignment validation
statement: The Cortex-M3 simulation stress shall check callee-saved state across blocking SVC and integer register plus NZCV state across interrupt-only regions, including injected mismatch detection and PSP padding.
rationale: Arithmetic workloads do not explicitly exercise every saved register or the exception alignment flag.
acceptance: Distinct canaries pass, injected r7 mismatch returns zero, ticks progress in the positive interrupt harness, and four-byte PSP alignment produces the hardware padding flag.
verification: Three QEMU timer shifts per configured stress image.
configuration: Assembly harnesses preserve AAPCS caller state and avoid C calls on a deliberately misaligned stack.
resource_budget: No heap; validation-only stack frames removed from ordinary images when unreferenced.
finding: Simulation coverage only, not MCU qualification or complete instruction-state proof.

title: ARM timer catch-up and rollover variants
statement: ARM simulation shall exercise masked multi-period timer catch-up, an initial 32-bit counter rollover with unchanged reload modulus, and varied queue capacity and tick rate.
rationale: Pending IRQ bits do not count missed periods and short timer reloads break software wrap extension.
acceptance: Ticks remain unchanged while masked then catch up within a counter deadline; near-wrap and faster-tick presets pass finite message and semaphore workloads.
verification: QEMU normal, near-wrap and faster-tick runs with retained logs.
configuration: CMSDK timer initial value configurable separately from full 32-bit reload; stress follows configured tick rate.
resource_budget: No dynamic firmware storage; variant queue capacity fixed at compilation.
finding: Counter extension still requires serialized reads more often than a full 32-bit period; no hardware timing guarantee.

title: Reproducible IPC models and discriminating ARM witnesses
statement: IPC verification shall include reproducible reference-state campaigns, exhaustive three-waiter ordering variants, and ARM witnesses that distinguish first-handler catch-up and live-window interruption.
rationale: A passing throughput test may miss order, detachment or interrupt-window failures; weak catch-up tests can pass single-tick accounting.
acceptance: Four seeds cover 600000 operations at three capacities;1296 waiter campaigns cover priorities, ties, expiry and changes; ARM records live-window PC, first elapsed count, preload and extended-time continuity.
verification: Host CTest and actual ARM QEMU campaigns with retained logs.
configuration: Fixed-capacity host oracles; optional ARM stress witness hooks default off outside stress presets.
resource_budget: No heap or TCB growth in ordinary firmware; stress-only observer state documented.
finding: Panel150 test-discrimination findings addressed; host checks are single-CPU models, not SMP or hardware evidence.

title: Optional host memory analysis and fail-closed symbol audits
statement: Native C++ host fixtures shall support optional ASan/UBSan and separate Valgrind Memcheck execution; firmware name audits shall reject empty or stripped symbol evidence and bound compiler/audit subprocesses.
rationale: Static analysis and target symbol checks do not expose all host memory defects, while absent symbols cannot support a name-based no-heap claim.
acceptance: Separate presets instrument native C++ or add finite Memcheck variants; both reject firmware configurations; stripped compiler fixture and symbol-presence self-tests pass; tool subprocess failures remain failures.
verification: Actual sanitizer/Memcheck CTest and ARM/RV32 compiler contracts.
configuration: CMake native checks and XDoc C# bounded executor; no custom Python tooling.
resource_budget: No target heap, RAM fields or runtime instrumentation; host model results do not qualify firmware.
finding: Known-symbol audit remains a limited check against recognizable allocation paths, not proof against arbitrary renamed/custom allocators.

title: Retained evidence and controlled analyzer detection gates
statement: Engineering checkpoints shall retain explicitly selected passing logs, manifests and audited unstripped images with bounded hash verification; controlled invalid-memory probes shall demonstrate specific analyzer rejection.
rationale: Ignored transient evidence can disappear and passing workloads alone do not show that analyzer failure gates are effective.
acceptance: Native C# collector rejects traversal, links, overwrite, size/count excess and changed/unlisted/duplicate inputs; round-trip/tamper self-tests pass; ASan, UBSan and Memcheck probes require intended diagnostic plus failure.
verification: Native evidence self-tests, actual controlled-failure gates and final package verification.
configuration: XDoc C# Native AOT collector with bounded inputs; probe output captured by shared bounded executor.
resource_budget: No firmware services or RAM; intentionally invalid host probe excluded from ordinary builds.
finding: Hashes support consistency rather than authenticity; retained simulation/host evidence is not board qualification or certification.

title: Optional portable DMA staging and quarantine implementation
statement: An optional DMA module shall serialize thread callers over one active transfer per channel using boot-reserved exclusive staging and explicit BSP address/cache/quiescence contracts, without retaining application-buffer pointers.
rationale: Unknown hardware stop semantics must not expose temporary caller storage to late DMA or force DMA storage into the nano kernel.
acceptance: DMA defaults off and adds no kernel fields; TX copies before launch; RX copies only after quiescent completion; stale tickets cannot release new transfers; uncertain abort quarantines until positive stop proof; host ownership tests pass.

title: Portable source handoff and dependency diagnosis

title: Critical section measurement coverage

verification: Combine compiler stack usage, call-chain review and target watermark fixtures including boot and fault paths.

statement: The release gate shall compare disabled-feature firmware against enabled firmware using identical toolchains and application behavior.
rationale: Optional source compilation does not guarantee that associated static storage disappears.

title: Timing units provenance
statement: Every timing result shall carry target frequency, counter width, conversion rule and measurement origin.
rationale: Host elapsed time and simulated timer advancement were previously easy to confuse.
acceptance: Changing frequency without regenerating the profile rejects qualification; host seconds cannot populate target-time fields.
verification: Exercise two clock profiles and counter wrap with known interval fixtures.
